title: Congruence and similarity
lede: Same shape and size, or same shape at a different scale. The ideas behind blueprints, maps, model trucks and measuring a tree with its shadow.

sections.md:
## Congruent: identical copies
Two figures are **congruent** (≅) if one can be moved onto the other by **sliding, flipping or turning**, with no stretching. All matching sides and all matching angles are equal.

To prove two **triangles** congruent, you don't need all six parts. These shortcuts are enough:

| Shortcut | What must match |
|---|---|
| **SSS** | all three sides |
| **SAS** | two sides and the angle **between** them |
| **ASA** | two angles and the side **between** them |
| **AAS** | two angles and a side **not** between them |
| **HL** | (right triangles only) hypotenuse and one leg |

**These don't work:**
- **AAA**: same angles can come in any size (that's similarity, not congruence).
- **SSA**: two sides and a non-included angle can make two different triangles.

sections.q: Two triangles have all three angles equal. Are they congruent?
options: Not necessarily: one could be a bigger copy

sections.md:
## CPCTC
Once you prove two triangles congruent, every other matching part is equal too: **Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent.** Proofs often prove triangles congruent as a stepping stone, then use CPCTC to get the side or angle they actually wanted.

## Similar: same shape, different size
Two figures are **similar** (∼) when all angles match and all side lengths are in the **same ratio**, called the **scale factor** k.

For triangles, shortcuts again:

| Shortcut | What must hold |
|---|---|
| **AA** | two angles match (the third must too) |
| **SSS∼** | all three side ratios are equal |
| **SAS∼** | two side ratios equal and the angle between them matches |

**Set up a proportion with matching sides:** small ÷ big = small ÷ big.

sections.title: The shadow trick
sections.problem: You're 6 ft tall and cast a 4 ft shadow. At the same moment, a light pole casts a 20 ft shadow. How tall is the pole?
steps: The Sun hits both at the same angle, and both stand straight up: the triangles are similar (AA).
height ÷ shadow is the same: 6/4 = h/20.
sections.answer: **30 ft.** Ancient Greek mathematician Thales is said to have measured the height of a pyramid this way.

sections.md:
## Scale factor: lengths, areas, volumes
If a figure is scaled by **k**:

| Measure | Multiplies by |
|---|---|
| lengths (sides, perimeter) | **k** |
| areas | **k²** |
| volumes | **k³** |

Double every dimension of a box (k = 2): its surface area becomes **4×**, its volume **8×**.

This is why giant animals can't just be scaled-up small ones: weight grows with volume (k³) while bone strength grows with cross-section area (k²). An ant scaled to elephant size would collapse.

sections.title: Area scaling
sections.problem: A trailer floor plan drawn at 1:50 has an area of 6 square inches on paper. What's the real area in square inches?
sections.answer: **15,000 in²**, about 104 ft². Forgetting to square the scale factor is the number one mistake here.

sections.label: Common traps
sections.md:
- **Matching the wrong sides.** Line up corresponding vertices first (the order in △ABC ≅ △DEF tells you A↔D, B↔E, C↔F).
- **SSA and AAA aren't congruence shortcuts.**
- **Scaling area by k instead of k².**
- **Congruent figures are similar** (k = 1), but similar figures usually aren't congruent.

practice.q: Which is **not** a valid congruence shortcut?
practice.why: Two different triangles can fit SSA.

practice.q: Two similar triangles: sides 3, 4, 5 and the bigger one's shortest side is 9. Its longest side?
A 5 ft person has a 3 ft shadow. A tree's shadow is 27 ft. Tree height?
Scale factor 3. Original area 10 cm². New area?
Scale factor 2. Original volume 50 cm³. New volume?
Two right triangles have equal hypotenuses and one equal leg. They're congruent by…
Two similar trailers: the small one has a 12 ft length and 300 ft³ volume. The big one is 24 ft. Its volume?
practice.why: k = 2, volume × 2³ = 8: 300 × 8 = **2,400 ft³**. Double the length, eight times the space.

practice.q: Two similar triangles have areas 16 and 36. If the smaller has a side of 8, what's the matching side of the larger?
practice.hint: Take the square root of the area ratio to get k.

practice.q: A map scale is 1 inch : 20 miles. A region is 3 in² on the map. Its real area is…
A 4 ft fence post casts a 6 ft shadow. A building casts a 90 ft shadow. How tall is the building?
practice.hint: Height to shadow is the same ratio for both.
